chunks: Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar al-Sabati from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who forgot to perform the Tawaf al-Nisa' until he returned to his family, he said: 'Upon him is a camel, which he slaughters between As-Safa and Al-Marwah.'

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A mature camel, used here as a specific measure of expiation
key_terms.بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: Between Safa and Marwah, the location for the sacrifice in this ruling
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa', the final circumambulation of the Kaaba performed before leaving Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for forgetting Tawaf al-Nisa' before leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* specifies that forgetting the final Tawaf (Tawaf al-Nisa') before departure incurs the penalty of a *badanah* (a mature camel), to be slaughtered between Safa and Marwah. This ruling highlights the juristic view that Tawaf al-Nisa' is a mandatory pillar (*rukn*) of Hajj, and its omission requires expiation even if done unintentionally, distinguishing it from mere sunnah acts.
